findings.source_passage: I twigged it, knew it; had had the gift, might readily have prophesied it—for when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 1, after 'Be sure the old Mogul has fixed him, too.'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence establishes Stubb's uncanny, half-comic claim to premonitory sight—'when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it'—which is interpretively significant as a motif of doomed foreknowledge running through the chapter and the novel; its omission flattens Stubb's voice and removes a thematic thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim or near-verbatim between 'the old Mogul has fixed him, too' and 'Well, Stubb': 'I twigged it, knew it; had had the gift, might readily have prophesied it—for when I clapped my eye upon his skull I saw it.'

findings.source_passage: (_Aside_) he's my superior, he has his too, if I'm not mistaken.
findings.source_locator: final paragraph, stage-direction aside after 'Mr. Starbuck? Aye, aye, sir'
findings.why_it_matters: The aside is a small but register-defining moment of dramatic irony—Stubb's sardonic acknowledgment that Starbuck too has been 'fixed' by Ahab; dropping it removes the closing comic-ironic punch of the monologue.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the aside marker and text: 'Aye, aye, sir—(Aside) he's my superior, he has his too, if I'm not mistaken.—Aye, aye, sir, just through with this job—coming.'

summary: The draft preserves all high-priority signature passages faithfully, including the song and the key comic-philosophic lines; two moderate omissions (the skull-premonition sentence and the closing aside) mildly flatten Stubb's voice but do not individually rise to regeneration level.
